canonical_statement: The study evaluated whether oral step-down therapy, compared with intravenous carbapenem therapy alone, affected venous catheter days and clinical outcomes in ESBL-producing E. coli urinary tract infections.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: This study evaluated whether treatment with oral step-down therapy compared with intravenous carbapenems alone ... impacted patient venous catheter days and clinical outcomes.

canonical_statement: This was a multicenter retrospective observational comparative cohort study conducted across six hospitals in one large health system.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: This was a multicenter, retrospective, observational, comparative cohort study conducted across six hospitals in a large health system.

canonical_statement: Eligible patients were adults hospitalized for at least 24 hours with at least one documented UTI symptom, ceftriaxone-resistant E. coli in urine, and at least one dose of meropenem or ertapenem from August 2022 through July 2025.

canonical_statement: The study excluded patients ineligible for oral therapy and patients with carbapenem-resistant E. coli, specified concomitant infections or conditions, chronic suppressive therapy, comfort/hospice care, pregnancy, or incarceration.
